subject: Catering Craft Practice
preamble: The general objectives of the Catering Craft Practice syllabus are to test candidates' acquisition of necessary skills and knowledge required for professional catering, food preparation, service, and enterprise operations.
aims: test candidates' level of development of professional attitude and skills;
test candidates' understanding of all food commodities in terms of cost, quality, and use;
test candidates' understanding of the methods of cooking and ability to produce a variety of dishes and drinks for various types of occasions, establishments, and individuals;
test candidates' understanding of dietary adequacies and procedures for producing dishes;
test candidates' understanding and application of hygienic practices in handling food;
test candidates' acquisition of necessary skills required for the production of pastry and confectionery products;
test candidates' application of the methods of choosing, caring for, and storing kitchen equipment;
test candidates' knowledge of safety precautions in catering;
test candidates' enterprise skills in menu costing and planning.

examination_scheme.summary: There will be three papers: Papers 1, 2, and 3. Papers 1 and 2 will be combined in a 1½-hour composite paper.

papers.title: Multiple Choice Objectives
papers.details: Comprises forty multiple-choice objective questions covering the entire syllabus.

papers.title: Short Essay Questions
papers.details: Comprises six short essay questions out of which candidates will answer five.

papers.title: Alternative to Practical Test
papers.details: Alternative to practical test comprising five short-structured questions. Candidates are expected to answer all questions.

topics.title: 1. Hospitality Industry and Catering
topics.notes: Definitions of hospitality and catering; components of the hospitality industry.

topics.title: 2. Types of Catering Establishments
topics.notes: Types of catering establishments (e.g., hotel, restaurant, hospitality catering, outdoor catering, school, mobile catering); functions of catering establishments.

topics.title: 3. Culinary Terms
topics.notes: Culinary terms commonly used in catering; comprehensive glossary of culinary terms.

topics.title: 4. Safety Precautions in Catering
topics.notes: Types and causes of accidents; prevention and management of accidents; first aid procedures; firefighting equipment and uses.

topics.title: 5. Sanitation and Hygiene in Catering
topics.notes: Water sanitation; environmental sanitation; food safety practices; kitchen hygiene; personal hygiene.

topics.title: 6. Food Commodities and Principles of Cooking Methods
topics.notes: Food commodities (e.g., poultry, game, meat, fish, vegetables, fruits, dairy products, pulses, cereals, herbs, flavourings); methods of cooking including boiling (stocks, soups, sauces), roasting (fish, beef, poultry), grilling (fish, meat), and baking (pastry, confectionery).

topics.title: 7. Principles of Cooking and Practical Demonstrations
topics.notes: Principles underlying various cooking methods; preparation techniques for different food commodities; standard and local measurements.

topics.title: 8. Food and Beverage Service Personnel
topics.notes: Personnel roles in the food and beverage area; functions and responsibilities of food and beverage service staff.

topics.title: 9. Types of Food Service and Table Setting
topics.notes: Different types of food service (e.g., Guéridon, silver service, waiter service, vending, buffet, banquet service); types of covers; types of table laying and setting.

topics.title: 10. Alcoholic and Non-Alcoholic Drinks
topics.notes: Bar operations; classification and service of alcoholic beverages; classification and service of non-alcoholic beverages.

topics.title: 11. Costing and Control in Catering
topics.notes: Cost/sales analysis; dish costing calculations; portion control techniques and importance.

topics.title: 12. Types, Care, and Maintenance of Kitchen Equipment
topics.notes: Types and uses of large, mechanical, and small kitchen equipment; care, cleaning procedures, and maintenance of various kitchen equipment.

topics.title: 13. Principles and Types of Menu Planning
topics.notes: Meaning and scope of menus; factors affecting menu planning; types of menus (e.g., table d'hôte, à la carte, special occasion, breakfast, tea, dinner, supper, luncheon, carte du jour, plat du jour).

topics.title: 14. Special Menus and Accompaniments
topics.notes: Meal planning for vegetarians, vulnerable groups, and manual or sedentary workers; food accompaniments and table accompaniments.
